# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Doi_2017_nc6004"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Doi_2017_nc6004"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-017-3254-4> (open access,
  PMC5344954). No supplementary material is published.

NC-6004 is cisplatin incorporated into polymeric micelles. Doi 2017 pooled
total and free (ultrafilterable) plasma platinum (Pt) from its Japanese
phase I study (NC-6004-003, with gemcitabine from cycle 2) with the UK
monotherapy phase I study NC-6004-001 (Plummer 2011,
<https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2011.6>), and linked free Pt to the estimated
glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) through an indirect-response model:

* Micellar Pt: two compartments (`central_np`, `peripheral1_np`; V1, V2, Q),
  eliminated by CL, with power body-weight effects on CL and V1 (Table 3).
* Free Pt: two compartments (`central`, `peripheral1`; Vm1, Vm2, Qm),
  eliminated by CLm. The micellar clearance is the only input to free Pt.
* Total Pt (`Cc_np`) is reported on the ICP scale; samples assayed by atomic
  absorption spectrometry (AAS, most of the UK study) read 1.69-fold higher
  (`ASSAY_AAS = 1`).
* eGFR (Methods Eq. 1): `d eGFR/dt = kin (1 - Imax Cf / (IC50 + Cf)) - kout
  eGFR`, with `kin = eGFR0 kout` and Cf the free Pt concentration in ng/mL.
* Methods Eq. 2: `Imax = Imax0 exp(-trend t) exp(eta_IOV)`, where t is the
  time since the first dose and the inter-occasion variability (IOV) changes
  at every administration (`OCC`).

The model runs in hours. Kout and the Imax trend are printed per day in
Table 4 and are divided by 24 in the model file.

# Population

Twelve Japanese patients (10 male, 2 female; age 34-72 years; 60 or 90
mg/m^2; Table 1) and 17 UK patients (10 male, 7 female; age 40-80 years;
10-120 mg/m^2; Plummer 2011 Table 2) with advanced solid tumours. The PK
data set holds 546 concentrations (108 ICP total Pt from Japan, 42 ICP and
144 AAS total Pt from the UK, 252 free Pt from 28 patients). The eGFR model
used 8.1 (Japan) and 13.7 (UK) observations per patient on average. The
typical-value body weight is 67.8 kg (Table 3 footnote); body weight and BSA
distributions are not reported.

Every Table 3 90% confidence interval for an IIV is symmetric in CV^2 (for
example Qm 54.4 (22.2-73.7): 0.544^2 = 0.2959 against a CI midpoint of
(0.222^2 + 0.737^2) / 2 = 0.2962), which is the signature of an estimated
variance reported as `CV% = 100 sqrt(omega^2)`. The same convention is used
for Table 4, which prints no intervals.

# Helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Doi_2017_nc6004")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
pt_per_cis <- 195.08 / 300.05 # mg Pt per mg cisplatin

# Virtual adults: body weight around the 67.8 kg reference, DuBois BSA.
make_cohort <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(67.8), 0.18))
  ht <- rnorm(n, 168, 8)
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), WT = wt, BSA = 0.007184 * wt^0.425 * ht^0.725)
}

# NC-6004 every 21 days as a 1-h infusion, dose labelled as cisplatin
# equivalent mg/m^2 and given to the model as mg of Pt. Observation rows
# carry dvid = 1 so that every output is returned on them. OCC increments
# with each dose; a trailing evid = 2 row on a further occasion gives every
# subject at least two occasions, which rxode2 needs to draw the IOV per
# subject and occasion.
make_events <- function(cohort, dose_mgm2, n_dose, obs_h, assay_aas = 0) {
  tau <- 21 * 24
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
    amt <- dose_mgm2 * cohort$BSA[i] * pt_per_cis
    dose <- data.frame(
      time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau, amt = amt, dur = 1, evid = 1L,
      cmt = "central_np", dvid = NA_integer_, OCC = seq_len(n_dose)
    )
    obs <- data.frame(
      time = obs_h, amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_,
      dvid = 1L, OCC = pmin(n_dose, floor(obs_h / tau) + 1L)
    )
    end <- data.frame(
      time = max(obs_h) + 1, amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 2L, cmt = NA_character_,
      dvid = NA_integer_, OCC = n_dose + 1L
    )
    bind_rows(dose, obs, end) |>
      mutate(id = cohort$id[i], WT = cohort$WT[i], ASSAY_AAS = assay_aas)
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Structural checks

```{r structure}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
# An explicit-ODE model; rxode2 must not have replaced it with a linCmt() solve.
stopifnot(is.null(ui$linCmt))

# Closed forms for one typical 67.8 kg subject after 100 mg of Pt: all
# micellar Pt is cleared by CL, and all of it then passes through CLm, so
# AUC(total, ICP) = Dose / CL and AUC(free) = Dose / CLm.
ev <- make_events(data.frame(id = 1, WT = 67.8, BSA = 1), 100 / pt_per_cis, 1,
  obs_h = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, 0.1), seq(48, 20000, 2))))
)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
))
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
auc_np <- trap(typ$time, typ$Cc_np)
auc_free <- trap(typ$time, typ$Cc)
closed <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("AUC total Pt (mg*h/L)", "AUC free Pt (mg*h/L)"),
  simulated = c(auc_np, auc_free),
  closed_form = c(100 / 0.0687, 100 / 6.54)
)
knitr::kable(closed, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(closed$simulated / closed$closed_form - 1) < 0.01))

# Derived half-lives the Results quote: eGFR recovers to half the damage in
# about 4 days (ln 2 / Kout), and Imax halves by day 25.4 (ln 2 / trend).
stopifnot(
  abs(log(2) / 0.171 - 4.05) < 0.01,
  abs(log(2) / 0.0273 - 25.4) < 0.05
)
```

# Dose units: comparison with the UK study NCA (Plummer 2011 Table 5)

NC-6004 doses are labelled in cisplatin-equivalent mg/m^2, but the model
predicts Pt concentrations. Doi 2017 does not say which mass entered the data
set as the dose. The UK study's published non-compartmental analysis
(Plummer 2011 Table 5; total Pt by AAS, ultrafilterable Pt by ICP-MS) settles
it: dosing the Pt mass (x 0.650) reproduces the reported total-Pt AUC, while
dosing the cisplatin mass overpredicts it by about half at every dose level.

```{r dose-units}
plummer <- tribble(
  ~dose, ~n, ~cmax_tot, ~auc_tot, ~cmax_uf, ~auc_uf,
  10, 1, 5.70, 234, 0.009, 1.7,
  20, 1, 12.20, 492, 0.022, 2.5,
  40, 3, 25.9, 1135, 0.045, 4.7,
  60, 3, 29.9, 1354, 0.096, 13.2,
  90, 6, 60.8, 2836, 0.205, 22.6,
  120, 3, 85.4, 4377, 0.131, 22.9
)
# Typical subject, 1.8 m^2 (BSA is not reported for the UK cohort), total Pt
# on the AAS scale as in Plummer 2011.
typ_auc <- function(dose_mgm2, mass_factor) {
  ev <- make_events(data.frame(id = 1, WT = 67.8, BSA = 1.8), dose_mgm2, 1,
    obs_h = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, 0.1), seq(48, 20000, 2)))), assay_aas = 1
  )
  ev$amt[ev$evid == 1] <- ev$amt[ev$evid == 1] / pt_per_cis * mass_factor
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  trap(s$time, s$Cc_np)
}
units_chk <- plummer |>
  filter(n >= 3) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    ratio_pt = typ_auc(dose, pt_per_cis) / auc_tot,
    ratio_cisplatin = typ_auc(dose, 1) / auc_tot
  ) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(units_chk |> select(dose, n, auc_tot, ratio_pt, ratio_cisplatin),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Typical-value AUC(0-inf) of total Pt (AAS scale) divided by the Plummer 2011 mean."
)
gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
stopifnot(
  # Pt-mass dosing is centred on the published AUCs ...
  abs(log(gm(units_chk$ratio_pt))) < log(1.2),
  # ... and cisplatin-mass dosing is not.
  gm(units_chk$ratio_cisplatin) > 1.35
)
```

# NCA against Plummer 2011 (PKNCA)

```{r nca}
nca_obs <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504)
cohort_uk <- make_cohort(60, seed = 2011)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(lapply(plummer$dose, function(d) {
  ev <- make_events(cohort_uk, d, 1, obs_h = nca_obs, assay_aas = 1)
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(100 + d)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(d, "mg/m^2"), dose = d)
}))

nca_long <- sim_nca |>
  select(id, time, treatment, Cc_np, Cc) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc_np, Cc), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc_np", "Total Pt (AAS)", "Ultrafilterable Pt")) |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(nca_long, conc ~ time | analyte + treatment / id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = intervals))

sim_mean <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  group_by(analyte, treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
ref_nca <- bind_rows(
  plummer |> transmute(analyte = "Total Pt (AAS)", treatment = paste(dose, "mg/m^2"),
    cmax = cmax_tot, aucinf.obs = auc_tot),
  plummer |> transmute(analyte = "Ultrafilterable Pt", treatment = paste(dose, "mg/m^2"),
    cmax = cmax_uf, aucinf.obs = auc_uf)
)
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(sim_mean, ref_nca,
  by = c("analyte", "treatment"),
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Simulated cohort means (60 virtual patients per dose) against the",
  "Plummer 2011 Table 5 means (1-6 patients per dose)."
))
```

The 10 and 20 mg/m^2 cohorts of Plummer 2011 hold one patient each, and the
ultrafilterable-Pt values at 120 mg/m^2 come from one valid profile, so
starred rows at those doses compare a cohort mean with a single individual.
At 40, 90 and 120 mg/m^2 the total-Pt Cmax and AUC agree within about 20%.
The 60 mg/m^2 cohort is overpredicted (AUC by about a quarter, Cmax by about
40%); its observed mean AUC per mg/m^2 is the lowest of the four cohorts with
three or more patients. Ultrafilterable Pt agrees less well and without a
consistent direction (over at 40 mg/m^2, under at 90 mg/m^2); the observed
means themselves are not dose-proportional (AUC 4.7 at 40 and 13.2 h*ug/mL at
60 mg/m^2). The UK patients' BSA and weights are not reported, so the cohort
uses the 67.8 kg reference weight.

```{r nca-check}
chk <- sim_mean |>
  filter(analyte == "Total Pt (AAS)", PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  inner_join(ref_nca |> select(analyte, treatment, ref = aucinf.obs),
    by = c("analyte", "treatment")) |>
  filter(treatment %in% paste(c(40, 60, 90, 120), "mg/m^2")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / ref - 1))
stopifnot(abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 25)
```

# eGFR visual predictive check (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of the simulated change
in eGFR from baseline by dose level, over eight 21-day cycles. Simulated
observations carry the 8.8% proportional residual error at baseline and at
each time, as the change of an observed value from an observed baseline.

```{r fig2, fig.height = 6}
doses_fig2 <- c(10, 20, 40, 60, 90, 120)
obs_days <- 0:170
cohort_vpc <- make_cohort(100, seed = 2017)
sim_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(doses_fig2, function(d) {
  ev <- make_events(cohort_vpc, d, 8, obs_h = obs_days * 24)
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2000 + d)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
    mutate(dose = d)
}))
set.seed(42)
vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  mutate(obs = egfr * (1 + 0.088 * rnorm(n()))) |>
  group_by(dose, id) |>
  mutate(pch = 100 * (obs / first(obs) - 1)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(day = time / 24)
vpc_q <- vpc |>
  group_by(dose, day) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(pch, 0.1), p50 = median(pch), p90 = quantile(pch, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_q, aes(day)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p10), linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p90), linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0, 147, 21), linetype = 3, colour = "grey60") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose, "mg/m^2")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-60, 30)) +
  labs(x = "Days", y = "Change in eGFR (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Doi 2017 (10th, 50th and 90th percentiles).")
```

Figure 2's median curve falls to about -15% to -25% within the first week at
40-120 mg/m^2, recovers toward baseline over each cycle, and the dips shrink
from cycle to cycle as Imax declines; its 10th percentile reaches about -40%
to -50%. The simulation reproduces this shape. Its day-7 medians (table
below) deepen from about -13% at 10 mg/m^2 to between -20% and -35% at
60-120 mg/m^2, the deepest at 120 mg/m^2 somewhat below the figure, with 100
virtual patients per dose level.

```{r fig2-check}
d7 <- vpc |> filter(day == 7)
med_d7 <- d7 |> group_by(dose) |> summarise(p50 = median(pch))
knitr::kable(med_d7, digits = 1, caption = "Median change in eGFR (%) on day 7.")
stopifnot(
  # Figure 2 at 90 mg/m^2: median about -20% in the first week.
  with(med_d7, p50[dose == 90] < -10 && p50[dose == 90] > -40),
  # Dose-response: the median dip deepens from 10 to 90 mg/m^2.
  with(med_d7, p50[dose == 10] > p50[dose == 90])
)
```

# Acute kidney injury at 100 mg/m^2 (Figure 4)

Doi 2017 converted each simulated eGFR to serum creatinine (sCr) by assuming
the sCr ratio to baseline is the inverse of the eGFR ratio, drew baseline sCr
from N(0.772, 0.124) mg/dL, and graded KDIGO stages on day 7 (6 days after a
single 100 mg/m^2 dose): stage 1 = sCr increase of 0.3 mg/dL or 1.5-1.9-fold,
stage 2 = 2.0-2.9-fold, stage 3 = 3.0-fold or an increase above 4.0 mg/dL.

```{r fig4}
cohort_aki <- make_cohort(200, seed = 4)
ev_aki <- make_events(cohort_aki, 100, 1, obs_h = 144)
kdigo <- function(sim, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  scr0 <- rnorm(nrow(sim), 0.772, 0.124)
  ratio <- ifelse(sim$egfr > 0, sim$rbase / sim$egfr, Inf)
  scr <- scr0 * ratio
  stage <- ifelse(ratio >= 3 | scr - scr0 > 4, 3,
    ifelse(ratio >= 2, 2, ifelse(ratio >= 1.5 | scr - scr0 >= 0.3, 1, 0))
  )
  100 * as.numeric(table(factor(stage, 0:3))) / length(stage)
}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(44)
aki_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_aki, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  filter(time == 144)

# Sensitivity: the same model with Imax bounded at 1, the range the paper
# states for Imax (0 < Imax < 1) but Eq. 2 does not enforce.
mod_cap <- mod |>
  rxode2::model(imax_t <- min(1, imax * exp(-imax_exp_kdes * tfirst) * exp(etaiov_limax)))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(44)
aki_cap <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cap, ev_aki, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  filter(time == 144)

aki <- data.frame(
  stage = c("No AKI", "Stage 1", "Stage 2", "Stage 3"),
  `Doi 2017 NC-6004 (Fig. 4)` = c(68, 22, 9, 1),
  `Simulated, Eq. 2 as printed` = kdigo(aki_sim, 5),
  `Simulated, Imax capped at 1` = kdigo(aki_cap, 5),
  `Cisplatin, Bhat 2015` = c(32.2, 33.0, 23.6, 11.2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(aki, digits = 1, caption = paste(
  "Replicates Figure 4 of Doi 2017 (percent of patients by KDIGO stage;",
  "Doi 2017 values read from the figure, cisplatin values from the cited",
  "observational cohort, 158 of 233 patients with AKI)."
))
aki |>
  pivot_longer(-stage, names_to = "source", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(stage, pct, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Patients (%)", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

The simulated stage 1 and 2 fractions are close to Figure 4, and NC-6004
produces far less AKI than cisplatin, as the paper concludes. Stage 3 is the
exception: Eq. 2 as printed gives `r round(aki[4, 3], 1)`% against the
paper's 1%, and correspondingly fewer patients without AKI. The excess comes
from occasions on which the log-normal IOV pushes Imax above 1 (at the first
dose this happens on `r round(100 * pnorm(-log(0.851), sd = 0.531, lower.tail = FALSE), 0)`%
of occasions): the production term `kin (1 - Imax Cf / (IC50 + Cf))` then
turns negative, and here `r round(100 * mean(aki_sim$egfr < 0), 1)`% of the
simulated patients have a negative eGFR on day 7.
Bounding Imax at 1, the range the paper states, lowers stage 3 to a few
percent but does not reach 1% either, and neither variant matches all four
bars, so the form the authors used for this simulation cannot be recovered
from the paper. The model file keeps Eq. 2 as printed, the form that was
estimated.

```{r fig4-check}
stopifnot(
  # NC-6004 at 100 mg/m^2 leaves most patients without AKI ...
  aki$`Simulated, Eq. 2 as printed`[1] > 45,
  # ... and far more of them than cisplatin does.
  aki$`Simulated, Eq. 2 as printed`[1] > aki$`Cisplatin, Bhat 2015`[1] + 10,
  # The documented stage-3 excess of Eq. 2 as printed over Figure 4.
  aki$`Simulated, Eq. 2 as printed`[4] > 3
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose mass.** The dose enters the model as mg of Pt: the labelled
  cisplatin-equivalent dose times 195.08 / 300.05 = 0.650. The paper does not
  state this; the Plummer 2011 NCA of the UK patients pooled in this analysis
  fits Pt-mass dosing and rejects cisplatin-mass dosing (section "Dose units").
* **Free-Pt input.** Table 3 has no release parameter other than CL, so all
  micellar clearance enters the free-Pt central compartment. Any fraction of
  CL not forming free Pt is absorbed into the apparent Vm1, Vm2, CLm and Qm.
* **Total Pt.** Total Pt is predicted as micellar central Pt only, as the
  two-compartment model fitted to total Pt describes it. Adding the free-Pt
  concentration would change it by under 1% (free Pt peaks at about 0.3% of
  total Pt), well inside the 17% residual
  error.
* **Imax above 1.** Eq. 2 multiplies Imax0 = 0.851 by `exp(eta_IOV)` with a
  53.1% CV, so Imax exceeds 1 on about 38% of occasions at the first dose
  (fewer later, as Imax declines), although the text and Table 4 state 0 < Imax < 1. The equation
  is kept as printed; see the Figure 4 section for the consequence (negative
  eGFR in a few percent of simulated subjects at 100 mg/m^2, and a stage-3
  AKI fraction several times the published one). Users who need a bounded effect can replace the
  `imax_t` line with `min(1, ...)` as in that section.
* **Time base of Imax.** `t_j` in Eq. 2 is taken as the time since the first
  NC-6004 dose (`tafd()`); occasions start at each administration.
* **IIV scale.** CV% is read as `100 sqrt(omega^2)` for both tables, as the
  Table 3 confidence intervals show (Source trace). Table 4 prints no
  intervals, so its IC50 variance (211.7% CV, omega^2 = 4.48) carries the same
  reading by assumption; the log-normal reading (omega^2 = 1.70) changes the
  simulated AKI fractions by only a few percentage points.
* **Covariates screened, not retained.** Ethnicity (Japanese vs Caucasian) on
  CL, baseline eGFR on CL and volume, and prophylactic hydration on the eGFR
  model are recorded in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Body weight is log-normal around the 67.8 kg reference
  (18% CV) and BSA is computed by DuBois from a simulated height; neither
  distribution is reported. The Figure 4 simulation in the paper does not
  state its cohort; the same virtual adults are used here.
* **Assay.** The paper describes the total-Pt AAS conversion as 'AA to ICP'
  with a fold of 1.69 and states AAS values were about 70% higher than ICP;
  the model therefore multiplies the ICP-scale prediction by 1.69 for AAS rows.
